Football Chess, open play. The 14 files a through n run left to right. Rank 17 is at the top, rank 1 at the bottom. White attacks the top, Black the bottom. Each goal is beyond files f through i. The boxes cover files e–j and ranks 1–3 or 15–17. White defends the bottom box, Black the top.
K is keeper, Q queen, N knight, R rook, B bishop and P pawn. A trailing digit is a player identifier. Light pieces belong to White and dark pieces to Black. The shooter carries the ball. On diagrams gold marks the shooter and two possible goal files, and teal marks the defending keeper. All unoccupied cells are empty.
For these ordinary shots the defending keeper starts in its own box. It can hold on its current square or react by stepping one square horizontally, vertically or diagonally into an empty on-board square. It may step outside its box. It cannot enter the opposing box or end on another piece. Chess check, attack maps and interceptions impose no additional restrictions on that step.

Attacking team: black. Two available goal files: g and i.

Ball carrier: black-Q. Occupied squares: black-K h16, black-Q i2, white-K h2, white-R1 f3, white-R2 f2, white-B1 h4, white-B2 g3, white-N1 h3, white-P2 k2, white-Q e3, white-N2 k1, white-P1 d3.

Choose the strongest immediate shot. If a single file is declared, the keeper knows the target and minimizes scoring probability. With disguise the keeper commits once, then the two files are equiprobable: minimize the average across targets for the same keeper reply. The shooter maximizes the resulting chance.
Guarding near the shot segment reduces scoring, especially when aligned and able to reach it in flight. A queen’s path can be body-blocked; a knight jumps over other pieces. Each opposing body whose square interior the shot segment crosses multiplies scoring probability by 0.55. A keeper inside its own box uses save coverage instead of body blocking. A keeper who stepped out loses save coverage and can body-block an ordinary shot. Ignore future rebounds and passes.
Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Select one option. Return its one-based number in option_id.
1. Declare file i
2. Disguise g/i
3. Declare file g

Respond with exactly one JSON object of the form {"option_id":1}, using the number of your chosen option.

Guarding near the shot segment reduces scoring, especially when aligned and able to reach it in flight. A queen’s path can be body-blocked; a knight jumps over other pieces. Each opposing body whose square interior the shot segment crosses multiplies scoring probability by 0.55. A keeper inside its own box uses save coverage instead of body blocking. A keeper who stepped out loses save coverage and can body-block an ordinary shot. Ignore future rebounds and passes.
Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Choose the strongest immediate shot. If a single file is declared, the keeper knows the target and minimizes scoring probability. With disguise the keeper commits once, then the two files are equiprobable: minimize the average across targets for the same keeper reply. The shooter maximizes the resulting chance.
Guarding near the shot segment reduces scoring, especially when aligned and able to reach it in flight. A queen’s path can be body-blocked; a knight jumps over other pieces. Each opposing body whose square interior the shot segment crosses multiplies scoring probability by 0.55. A keeper inside its own box uses save coverage instead of body blocking. A keeper who stepped out loses save coverage and can body-block an ordinary shot. Ignore future rebounds and passes.
Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Guarding near the shot segment reduces scoring, especially when aligned and able to reach it in flight. A queen’s path can be body-blocked; a knight jumps over other pieces. Each opposing body whose square interior the shot segment crosses multiplies scoring probability by 0.55. A keeper inside its own box uses save coverage instead of body blocking. A keeper who stepped out loses save coverage and can body-block an ordinary shot. Ignore future rebounds and passes.
Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Each opposing body whose square interior the shot segment crosses multiplies scoring probability by 0.55. A keeper inside its own box uses save coverage instead of body blocking. A keeper who stepped out loses save coverage and can body-block an ordinary shot. Ignore future rebounds and passes.
Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.

Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Reference formula for these shots, with file a=0,...,n=13 and y=board rank. S is shooter center; T is the target file center at rank 17.5 or 0.5. L=|T-S|, u=(T-S)/L, d=abs(Ty-Sy). C(z)=clamp(z,0,1). Let w be the angle subtended at S by the two physical posts x=4.5 and 8.5 at Ty, w0=2*atan(2/d), h=C((w in degrees-45)/45). In-box on-target probability A=clamp(0.98*1.15*exp(-0.018*L-0.06*max(0,L-3)^2)*(0.65+0.35*d/L)*(0.1+0.9*C(w/w0)^1.5)*(1+0.25*h*h*(3-2*h))*(1.15 if S is on g/h else 1),0.01,0.98). Use consistent angle units in w/w0.
For keeper reply center K, v=(K-S) dot u, l=clamp(v,0,L), c=|K-(S+l*u)|, t=l/6, b=keeper distance in ranks from its own end rank. Inside the box: reach=0.4+1.3*max(0,t-0.15); ready=0.9*(1-exp(-(0.35+t+b*abs(uy)/6)/0.45)); dive=ready*exp(-(c/reach)^2) if v>=0 else 0. For 0<v<L, rush=0.2*C(b/2)*max(0,1-(|K-S|/6)^2)*exp(-(c/0.9)^2), otherwise rush=0. Save=clamp(dive+(1-dive)*rush,0,0.9). Outside the box Save=0, and A is normal pass accuracy: 1 through ten Chebyshev steps to the goal target at rank 18 or 0, then minus 0.1 per extra step down to 0.25. Goal probability equals A*(1-Save)*0.55^(number of blocking bodies), with zero blockers for a knight.
